Hi team! Hope you're having a good week over there. I've been using Inkwell for about eight months now to keep track of grad school research, recipe ideas, and honestly my entire brain dump, and it's become the app I open first thing every morning, coffee in hand. I wanted to share something I keep running into. My notes have started to multiply — I think I'm past 600 now — and a lot of them are related to each other in ways that aren't obvious just from folders or tags. Like, my note on 'sourdough starter troubleshooting' actually connects to a note from three months ago about kitchen humidity that I wrote for a totally different reason, and right now the only way I remember that connection exists is because I happen to have a good memory for weird trivia. What I'd love is some way to type something like [[humidity]] inside a note and have it automatically link to any other note with that word or phrase, plus maybe a little map or web view where I could see how everything connects visually. I've seen a few other note apps do something like this and it genuinely changes how you think while you write, because you start noticing patterns you'd have otherwise missed. I know tagging exists already and I do use it, but tags feel more like folders in disguise, whereas what I'm picturing is more organic, more like the notes are talking to each other. Anyway, no rush on this, I just wanted to plant the idea since I think a lot of your long-time users are hitting the same wall I am once their note count gets this high. Thanks for reading this far, and thanks for building something I actually enjoy using every day!

Let's just say Huddleview and I have reached the end of our situationship. I want to be fair here: the video quality was fine, the screen share never glitched on me, and whoever designed your virtual backgrounds deserves a raise. But none of that changes where we've landed. Back in March you bumped the Business tier from $34 a month to $49 a month with about a week's notice, buried in an email whose subject line was literally 'Exciting updates!' — which, respectfully, is not the phrase I'd use for a 44% price hike. I grumbled, I complained to my co-founder, I even opened a support ticket that got answered with a canned line about 'added value.' I let it go and kept paying because switching tools mid-quarter is its own special hell. But here we are again, six months later, and I just got notified about another jump, this time to $61. That's the actual last straw, not the first one. I don't need a discount, I don't need a retention specialist to call me and recite a script about how much you value me — I've heard that movie before. What I need is for my workspace, three seats, going by the name Larkspur Consulting, to stop auto-renewing at the end of this billing cycle and for the account to be fully closed out after that, no lingering trial mode, no 'we'll keep your data for 90 days just in case.' If there's a form for this I'll fill it out myself; I just want written confirmation it's actually done and that no further card charges are coming. Thanks in advance for making this the smoothest breakup of the two of us.

This would matter most for teams handling sensitive client files, which is most of our business.

Over the past fourteen months, our team has used Clearmetric as the primary reporting layer sitting on top of our internal event pipeline. For reference, our setup ingests roughly 2.3 million events per day across eleven distinct event types, feeding into six custom dashboards that our stakeholders check every Monday morning. We spent a significant amount of time in the first quarter configuring custom attribution windows, since the default seven-day lookback didn't match our sales cycle, and eventually settled on a 21-day window after testing against historical conversion data. The retention cohort view was particularly useful during that period, and I want to note for the record that the support engineer who helped us debug a timezone offset issue in March, a person named Priya if I recall the ticket correctly, did excellent work and resolved it within a day. We also appreciated the CSV export feature added last year, which we used heavily for board reporting. That said, our finance team finalized next year's budget last week, and analytics tooling of this kind did not make the cut given a broader shift toward consolidating vendors under a single company-wide BI contract starting in January. Given that, please make sure our workspace, org ID CM-8823, does not renew past the current contract term and that no further invoices are generated after December's cycle closes. I'll follow up separately regarding data export before the account closes, since we'll want to retain historical dashboards for our own archives. Thanks for the work your team has put in over the past year; the decision here is organizational rather than a reflection on the product itself.

I want to start by saying that I've genuinely enjoyed my three years with Fernwood, and I mean that sincerely, not as a preamble to a complaint, because there isn't one. When I first signed up back in 2023, I was mostly using it for grocery lists and half-formed blog post ideas, nothing serious. Over time it grew into something closer to a personal archive: journal entries, book notes organized by author, a folder of recipes converted from my grandmother's handwritten cards, and an embarrassingly detailed log of every plant I've managed to keep alive or, more often, kill. I particularly liked the daily note template you rolled out two summers ago, and the tagging system has held up well even as my note count crept past two thousand. I also want to mention, because I think feedback in both directions matters, that your support team helped me recover a folder I'd accidentally deleted back in April, and that alone earned a lot of goodwill from me. All of that said, I started a new position in November that comes with a strict policy against storing any work-adjacent notes in personal, non-approved software, and while most of what's in my account is personal rather than professional, enough of it blurs the line that I'd rather not risk it. So, with genuine reluctance, I'd like to close my account and stop the subscription from renewing next month, once I've finished exporting everything to a local backup, which I understand takes a few days to process on your end. I'll reach out again once the export is confirmed complete so we can finalize the account closure from there.
